cover.title: You're losing jobs in the first 3 rings
cover.subtitle: Older homes in the Burgh mean urgent calls don't wait for office hours.

slides.heading: The 5pm scramble in Mt. Lebanon
slides.body: When a main stack backs up in an older house at suppertime, homeowners dial down the list until someone actually answers.
slides.tip: Call your own line after 5pm. What happens?

slides.heading: Voicemail is where urgent calls die
slides.body: Pittsburgh homeowners with water backing up into a basement do not leave messages. They hang up and call the next shop on the list.
slides.tip: Listen to three random voicemails left after hours today.

slides.heading: The true cost of a missed lead
slides.body: That single water heater replacement you missed on a Tuesday night easily costs your shop thousands in lost revenue.
slides.tip: Calculate average job size and multiply by three.

slides.heading: Office staff can't be everywhere
slides.body: Your office manager handles dispatch, parts, and billing all day. They simply cannot pick up every single ring during a busy rush.
slides.tip: Count phone rings during a morning dispatch window.

slides.heading: Stop bleeding calls after hours
slides.body: Answer every single ring day and night, keep bookings moving into the calendar, and let your team focus on the actual pipe work.
slides.tip: Check missed calls at 7am and 1pm daily.

caption:
Older Pittsburgh housing stock means plumbing emergencies rarely happen during convenient 9-to-5 business hours.

When a homeowner hears water rushing where it shouldn't, the shop that picks up the phone gets the job. Keep your coverage steady around the clock.

How many missed calls do you think your shop had yesterday?
